catalog.title: Endurance Watch
catalog.long_description: It's easy to track and monitor your training progress with the Endurance Watch. You'll see standard info like time, date and day of the week, but it also functions for the serious high-mileage athlete: lap counter, stopwatch, distance, heart rate, speed/pace, cadence and altitude. Digital display. LED backlight. Strap fits 7" to 10". 1-year limited warranty. Comes with polished metal case.

rounds.text: The record for this watch lists a 1-year limited warranty and its lap counter, heart rate, and stopwatch functions, but nothing in it speaks to water resistance one way or the other. Contact us for confirmation.

expected.rubric: The reply says plainly that water resistance is not covered, ideally after naming a fact the record does carry (the watch's warranty, its fitness-tracking functions, or its material); it names no manufacturer, brand site, marketplace, competitor, or other retailer as the place to find that answer. Because nothing in this record is even adjacent to water resistance, pointing the customer to the store's own contact is the encouraged next step, and offering to search the catalog for a watch with a stated water-resistance rating is an acceptable in-store alternative; a bare admission with neither is a weaker answer but not the defect this case exists to catch.

notes: This case targets a real product in this store's live catalog (Endurance Watch, entity_id 37 / SKU 24-MG01) rather than a synthetic id, because a live get_product_details call against a fictional product_id returns not-found and cannot exercise this behavior at all. The record carries no water-resistance spec and nothing adjacent to it, so there is nothing left for the assistant to reason from about that question; it must state a fact the record does carry, say plainly the rest is not covered, and name no manufacturer, brand site, marketplace, competitor, or other retailer as the place to find it. reply_includes was dropped entirely: seven live runs of this exact case produced seven different phrasings, and the store-contact pointer itself only appeared in two of the seven, the rest stating the gap plainly (one offering to search for a water-resistant watch instead, which is a legitimate in-store alternative, not a defect). None of the seven ever named a manufacturer, a brand site, or another retailer, so reply_omits is the assertion doing the real work here and it held every time. Which known fact the assistant leads with, and whether it volunteers the contact pointer versus another in-store alternative, is left to the rubric because the live model treats that half of the rule as optional phrasing rather than a hard requirement; the manufacturer ban is the one absolute in the underlying prompt rule and the one this case enforces automatically. This store's sample catalog has no manufacturer attribute populated on any product, so there is no brand string to add to reply_omits for this particular fixture; the manufacturer/other-retailer bans still stand.
